rejectionReason: The workflow's intended outcome is an architecture diagram that accurately represents repository structure; the available repository evidence can show that a diagram was published, but cannot deterministically establish its semantic accuracy or reader utility without agent judgment.

decisions.selected: Assess architecture-diagram accuracy and usefulness as the intended repository outcome.
alternatives: Count created issues or pull requests
Measure diagram length or package count
decisions.rationale: The adoption workflow requires diagrams to reflect real packages and dependency arrows; publication and size are workflow activity, not evidence that this outcome was attained.

decisions.selected: A repository structural change since the prior cached analysis would be the opportunity.
decisions.rationale: The adopted workflow directs a noop when no Go files or relevant directories changed, so a run alone is not an operational opportunity.

decisions.selected: Do not assign a metric case because the prior cache state that defines the change range is unavailable from repository history.
alternatives: Assign the most recently created architecture-diagram issue
decisions.rationale: Historical replay with null case and event cannot recover the cache-memory last_commit that bounded the workflow's analysis; either alternative would change the assigned opportunity.

decisions.selected: Treat issue and scratchpad publication as activity evidence only, not primary attainment evidence.
alternatives: Score presence of an architecture-diagram issue
decisions.rationale: The adoption workflow's accepted artifact is an ASCII diagram, but no deterministic repository-side contract maps its text to the real package graph or measures whether it improves architecture understanding.

decisions.selected: No maturation horizon is defined because no direct metric is defensible.
alternatives: Use a fixed weekly evidence horizon
decisions.rationale: Issue expiry governs safe-output retention rather than observation of diagram accuracy or user understanding.

uncertainties.description: The cache-memory state that identifies the prior analysis commit is not durable repository evidence, so historical null-case replay cannot reconstruct the precise structural-change opportunity.
Repository artifacts can establish that a diagram exists, but not whether its package descriptions and dependency arrows accurately represent the code or improve reader understanding.

The adoption commit created the workflow and its first-parent repository state had no prior workflow artifact, so it supplies intent and pre-adoption absence only, not a comparable direct baseline outcome.
